label: conj:q-geometric-langlands
title: $q$-Geometric Langlands correspondence
html:
Conjecture. q-Geometric Langlands correspondence

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with brane curve X, quantum gauge group G_q, and q-Langlands dual \check{G}_q (q-Langlands dual).

The correspondence below is the substrate-level analogue of geometric Langlands: it relates \mathcal{D}_q-modules on the quantum bundle stack to quasi-coherent sheaves on the moduli of local systems for the q-dual, so that spectral data on one side controls automorphic data on the other. At the classical value q = 1 it specialises to the ordinary geometric Langlands equivalence (property 5 below), which fixes the target that the deformed statement must recover; the parameter q then deforms that equivalence across the non-torsion locus of the substrate. With this anchor in hand, the q-Geometric Langlands correspondence asserts the existence of an equivalence of \infty-categories:

  \mathbb{L}_q \colon
  \mathcal{D}_q\text{-}\mathrm{mod}(\mathrm{Bun}_{G_q}(X))
  \xrightarrow{ \sim }
  \mathrm{QCoh}(\mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X)).

This equivalence is parametrised by the non-torsion locus q \in \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}(k) and satisfies five properties:

  1. Hecke compatibility: For every q-Hecke operator \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)} (q-Hecke operator), \mathbb{L}_q intertwines the action on the left with the action of V_\lambda^{(q)} on \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X):

      \mathbb{L}_q \circ \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)}
  \simeq
  V_\lambda^{(q)}(-)_x \otimes \mathbb{L}_q.

    This is the eigensheaf-matching condition: intertwining the q-Hecke action with tensoring by V_\lambda^{(q)} is what makes \mathbb{L}_q a Langlands correspondence rather than an arbitrary equivalence of categories.

  2. Fibre-functor factorisation: the equivalence factors through the fibre functor \tau:

      \mathbb{L}_q = \tau^* \circ \mathbb{L}_q^{\mathrm{Tannakian}}.

    where \mathbb{L}_q^{\mathrm{Tannakian}} is determined by Tannaka--Krein reconstruction for \check{G}_q. Routing the equivalence through \tau keeps it compatible with the observation frame, so that the dual group is recovered from its representation category rather than posited independently.

  3. q-Oper locus: the equivalence \mathbb{L}_q restricts to a bijection between q-opers (q-oper) and q-Hecke eigensheaves (q-Hecke eigensheaf):

      \mathrm{Op}_{\check{G}_q}(X)  \hookrightarrow 
  \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X)
  \quad\xrightarrow{\mathbb{L}_q^{-1}}\quad
  \{\text{$q$-Hecke eigensheaves}\}.

    This pins down which local systems arise as q-Hecke eigensheaves: the q-opers cut out the distinguished spectral parameters that the eigensheaves correspond to under \mathbb{L}_q.

  4. Kummer constraint: the equivalence \mathbb{L}_q is well-defined as a \mathbb{G}_m-family on the non-torsion locus \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}. At roots of unity q \in \mu_n the quantum dimension [n]_q = 0 vanishes, the Frobenius pairing degenerates, and \mathbb{L}_q degenerates. The obstruction (Kummer filtration) persists at all Kummer levels n \nmid \chi(A).

  5. Classical limit: as q \to 1, \mathbb{L}_q recovers the classical Geometric Langlands equivalence (classical limit).
